lessons.title: The Twelve Main Meridians
lessons.blurb_en: Why an acupuncture point on your foot can affect an organ in your torso — the logic of the twelve meridians.
lessons.blurb_zh: 為什麼腳上的一個穴位能影響到軀幹裡的一個臟腑——十二經絡背後的邏輯。
paras: Chinese medicine describes twelve main meridians, one connected to each of the six zang and six fu organs introduced in the last unit. Each meridian runs along either an arm or a leg, linking a limb to its associated organ deep inside the torso — the Lung meridian, for example, runs along the inner arm, and the Stomach meridian runs down the front of the leg. This is why an acupuncturist might work on a point far from where a symptom is felt: the meridian connects that distant point to the organ in question.

The twelve meridians are organized in a system of three yin and three yang meridians on each limb, six on the arms and six on the legs. Yin meridians generally run along the inner, more protected surface of a limb and connect to zang organs; yang meridians generally run along the outer surface and connect to fu organs. This is not an arbitrary naming choice — it follows the same yin-yang logic from earlier in this course: interior and storing (yin) versus exterior and processing (yang).

None of this needs to be memorized point by point to be useful. What matters is the underlying idea: the twelve meridians form one continuous, connected network rather than twelve separate, isolated lines, and qi is said to flow through all twelve in a fixed sequence over the course of a day, passing the "baton" from one meridian to the next. A blockage or weakness doesn't stay isolated in one line — it can affect the flow reaching every meridian downstream.
paras_zh: 中醫描述了十二條主要經絡，分別連結到上個單元介紹過的六臟六腑。每條經絡沿著一隻手臂或一條腿走，把一個肢體連結到它對應、深藏在軀幹裡的臟腑——舉例來說，肺經沿著手臂內側走，胃經沿著腿的前側往下走。這就是為什麼針灸師有時候會在離症狀感覺到的地方很遠的一個點上下針：經絡把那個遙遠的點，連結到相關的臟腑。
十二條經絡按照每個肢體三陰三陽的系統來組織，手臂上六條、腿上六條。陰經通常沿著肢體內側、比較受保護的表面走，連結到五臟；陽經通常沿著外側表面走，連結到六腑。這不是任意取的命名方式——它遵循的是這門課前面講過的同一套陰陽邏輯：內部、儲存性質（陰）對上外部、處理性質（陽）。
這一切不需要一個點一個點地背下來才有用。重要的是背後的概念：十二條經絡形成一個連續、彼此連結的網絡，而不是十二條各自獨立的線，而氣被認為在一天當中依照固定的順序流過全部十二條，把「接力棒」從一條經絡傳給下一條。一個地方的阻塞或虛弱，不會停留在孤立的一條線上——它可以影響到下游每一條經絡的氣血流動。

lessons.title: How Meridians Explain Referred Pain
lessons.blurb_en: Why a heart attack hurts down the arm — and how Chinese medicine mapped the same pattern centuries earlier.
lessons.blurb_zh: 為什麼心臟病發作會痛到手臂——以及中醫如何在幾世紀前就畫出同樣的模式。
paras: One of the clearest ways to make meridians feel less abstract is to connect them to something Western medicine already accepts: referred pain. A heart attack, for example, is well known in Western emergency medicine to sometimes cause pain that radiates down the left arm rather than staying in the chest — a connection modern medicine explains through shared nerve pathways. Chinese medicine had already mapped a very similar connection centuries earlier: the Heart meridian runs from the chest down the inner arm, and pain along that exact path has long been read as a sign of a heart-related pattern.

This kind of pattern shows up elsewhere too. Chinese medicine has long used the location of a headache as a diagnostic clue, because different meridians cross different parts of the head. Pain across the forehead is traditionally linked to the Stomach meridian; pain along the temples is linked to the Gallbladder meridian; pain at the very top of the head is linked to the Liver meridian. A patient describing exactly where a headache sits is, without knowing it, giving a meridian-based clue that a practitioner trained in this system knows how to read.

None of this claims that a headache location has only one possible cause, or that this reading replaces an actual examination. What it shows is that "referred pain" and "location-specific symptoms" are not exotic ideas unique to Chinese medicine — they are a shared observation that two very different medical traditions arrived at through different methods, and meridians are simply the map Chinese medicine built to organize that observation systematically.
paras_zh: 讓經絡感覺不那麼抽象的一個最清楚的方法，是把它們連結到西醫已經接受的一件事：牽涉痛。舉例來說，心臟病發作在西方急診醫學裡是眾所周知會有時候造成疼痛沿著左手臂放射，而不是只停留在胸口——現代醫學透過共享的神經路徑來解釋這個連結。中醫在好幾個世紀以前，就已經標出了一個非常類似的連結：心經從胸口一路走到手臂內側，沿著這條確切路徑出現的疼痛，長久以來被讀成心相關病證的一個徵象。
這種模式在別的地方也會出現。中醫長久以來把頭痛的位置當成一個診斷線索，因為不同的經絡穿過頭部的不同區域。橫跨前額的疼痛，傳統上跟胃經有關；太陽穴附近的疼痛，跟膽經有關；頭頂正中央的疼痛，跟肝經有關。一位病人描述頭痛確切位在哪裡，在自己不知情的狀況下，其實提供了一個以經絡為基礎的線索，讓受過這套系統訓練的醫師知道怎麼解讀。
這一切並不是在主張某個頭痛位置只可能有一個原因，也不是說這種解讀能取代真正的檢查。它顯示的是「牽涉痛」跟「位置特定的症狀」，並不是中醫獨有的異國情調概念——這是兩套非常不同的醫學傳統，透過不同的方法，共同抵達的一個觀察，而經絡只是中醫用來有系統地整理這個觀察所建構的地圖。

lessons.title: What Acupuncture Points Actually Are
lessons.blurb_en: A light switch, not the wiring itself — what an acupuncture point is, without naming or teaching any.
lessons.blurb_zh: 是開關，不是電線本身——穴位到底是什麼，但不指名、不教學任何一個穴位。
paras: An acupuncture point is best understood as a specific, mapped location along a meridian where the flow of qi is considered especially accessible — a place where stimulation reliably produces an effect somewhere else along that same meridian's path. There are roughly 360 commonly used points across the twelve main meridians, each with its own name, location, and traditional set of effects, built up through the same centuries of clinical observation that produced the meridian map itself.

A useful comparison is a light switch versus the wiring behind a wall. The meridian is the wiring — the path along which influence travels, mostly hidden. An acupuncture point is like a switch: a specific, accessible spot where a person can interact with that hidden system to produce an effect, without needing to see or touch the wiring itself. Just as flipping a switch in one room can turn on a light in a completely different room, stimulating a point on the foot can be intended to affect an organ deep in the torso.

This course will not name specific points or teach anyone to use them — locating and stimulating a point safely and appropriately is a skill that takes years of supervised training, and doing it incorrectly is not harmless. What matters here is understanding the concept clearly enough to make sense of what a practitioner is actually doing during treatment, and to know that acupuncture is a precise, trained skill — not a matter of poking anywhere that seems to hurt.
paras_zh: 一個穴位最好被理解成經絡上一個特定、已被標定出來的位置，在這個位置上，氣的流動被認為特別容易被觸及——一個刺激它就能可靠地在同一條經絡路徑上別的地方產生效果的地方。十二條主要經絡上，大約有 360 個常用穴位，每一個都有自己的名稱、位置，以及傳統上記錄的一套效果，是透過跟建構出經絡地圖同一個過程——好幾個世紀的臨床觀察——累積出來的。
一個有用的比喻是電燈開關跟牆壁後面的電線。經絡就是電線——影響力傳遞的路徑，大部分是隱藏起來的。一個穴位就像一個開關：一個特定、容易觸及的點，讓人可以跟那個隱藏的系統互動，產生一個效果，不需要看到或摸到電線本身。就像在一個房間按下開關，可以打開完全不同房間裡的燈一樣，刺激腳上的一個穴位，目的可能是要影響軀幹裡深處的一個臟腑。
這門課不會指名特定的穴位，也不會教任何人怎麼使用它們——安全且恰當地定位並刺激一個穴位，是需要好幾年受監督訓練的技能，做錯了並不是無害的。這裡重要的是把這個概念理解得夠清楚，好讓你看懂醫師在治療過程中實際在做什麼，也知道針灸是一項精確、受過訓練的技能——不是隨便哪裡覺得痛就往哪裡扎。

lessons.title: The Eight Extraordinary Vessels: The Meridian System's Reservoirs
lessons.blurb_en: Beyond the twelve main meridians, eight extra channels act less like roads and more like reservoirs feeding the whole system.
lessons.blurb_zh: 十二正經之外還有八條額外的通道，功能比較不像道路，比較像餵養整個系統的水庫。
paras: The twelve main meridians introduced earlier in this unit each belong to a specific organ, run through a specific limb, and follow a fixed daily sequence. Chinese medicine describes eight additional channels that don't follow any of those rules, called the "eight extraordinary vessels." They aren't matched to individual organs, and they don't carry qi in the same continuous, hand-to-organ relay described earlier — instead, they're traditionally compared to reservoirs, holding and releasing qi and blood to support the twelve regular meridians when needed, rather than being part of the everyday flow themselves.

Two of the eight carry particular weight because, unlike the other six, they have their own dedicated acupuncture points rather than only borrowing points from the twelve regular meridians. The Governing Vessel runs up the center of the back and is associated with all of the body's yang meridians, sometimes described as the "sea of yang." The Conception Vessel runs up the center of the front of the body and is associated with all of the yin meridians, sometimes described as the "sea of yin" — together forming a kind of central spine for the entire meridian system.

The reservoir comparison matters because it explains why these eight vessels come up specifically in discussions of chronic, long-standing conditions rather than sudden ones. A sudden problem is usually read through the twelve regular meridians, the way a delayed bus is read through the regular schedule rather than the emergency backup system. The eight extraordinary vessels are the backup system — rarely the first place a doctor looks, but the reserve that becomes relevant when the everyday network has been under strain for a long time.
paras_zh: 這個單元稍早介紹的十二正經，每一條都屬於一個特定的臟腑、走過一個特定的肢體、遵循一個固定的每日順序。中醫描述了八條不遵循這些規則的額外通道，叫做「奇經八脈」。它們沒有對應到個別的臟腑，也不像稍早描述的那種手到臟腑接力式的連續氣血運行——傳統上，它們更常被比喻成水庫，在需要的時候儲存並釋放氣血來支援十二正經，而不是本身就參與日常的循環。
八條裡有兩條特別有份量，因為跟其他六條不同，它們有自己專屬的穴位，不只是借用十二正經的穴位。督脈沿著背部正中線往上走，跟身體所有的陽經有關，有時被稱為「陽脈之海」。任脈沿著身體前方正中線往上走，跟所有的陰經有關，有時被稱為「陰脈之海」——兩者合起來，形成整個經絡系統的一種中軸脊柱。
水庫的比喻很重要，因為它解釋了為什麼這八條經脈特別會在討論慢性、長期的狀況時被提起，而不是突發的狀況。突發的問題通常透過十二正經來解讀，就像誤點的公車會透過正常班表來解讀，而不是透過緊急備援系統。奇經八脈是那套備援系統——很少是醫師第一個查看的地方，但當日常的網絡承受長期壓力時，它就是變得相關的那份儲備。

lessons.title: Why Pressing a Sore Spot Sometimes Helps
lessons.blurb_en: Not every useful point has a name or a fixed location — some are found simply by pressing until something hurts.
lessons.blurb_zh: 不是每個有用的點都有名字或固定位置——有些只是靠按壓，按到痛為止就找到了。
paras: An earlier lesson in this unit described acupuncture points as fixed, mapped locations along the twelve meridians, each with its own name and traditional set of effects. Chinese medicine also recognizes a second, much less formal category: points with no fixed location at all, found simply by pressing around an area until a person reacts to a tender spot. These are called "ashi points," a name that comes from the sound a person makes when the press finds the right place — roughly, "ah, yes, that's it."

An ashi point isn't marked on any traditional chart, doesn't have a name of its own, and can appear in a completely different spot from one person to the next, or even from one week to the next in the same person. What makes it worth treating isn't its location on a map — it's the local tenderness itself, read as a sign that qi and blood have become stuck in that specific spot, regardless of which meridian happens to run nearby.

This category matters for understanding acupuncture as a living practice rather than a fixed lookup table. Alongside points chosen because a chart says they affect a particular organ, a practitioner is also always working with what the body is showing right now, in real time, at that specific visit — the fixed map and the moment-to-moment finding work together rather than one replacing the other.
paras_zh: 這個單元稍早的一課，把穴位描述成沿著十二正經、固定、已被標定出來的位置，每一個都有自己的名字與傳統記錄的一套效果。中醫也承認第二個、正式程度低得多的類別：完全沒有固定位置的點，單純靠在一個區域周圍按壓，直到一個人對某個痠痛的點有反應而找到。這些被稱為「阿是穴」，這個名字來自按到對的地方時，一個人發出的聲音——大概就是「啊，對，就是這裡」。
阿是穴不會被標在任何傳統的圖表上，沒有自己的名字，而且可能在不同的人身上出現在完全不同的地方，甚至在同一個人身上，這週跟下週也可能不一樣。讓它值得被處理的，不是它在地圖上的位置——而是那個局部的痠痛本身，被讀成氣血在那個特定地點卡住的一個徵象，不管附近剛好經過的是哪一條經絡。
這個類別，對理解針灸是一種活的實踐，而不是一份固定的查詢表，很重要。除了因為圖表寫著會影響某個特定臟腑而選定的穴位之外，醫師也一直在處理身體此時此刻、在那次特定的看診當下所顯現出來的狀況——固定的地圖跟當下發現的東西是一起合作的，不是其中一個取代另一個。

lessons.title: Why Stretching Along a Meridian Feels Different
lessons.blurb_en: Why certain qigong and stretching movements trace the exact path of a meridian instead of a random shape.
lessons.blurb_zh: 為什麼某些氣功與伸展動作，走的正是一條經絡的路徑，而不是隨便一個形狀。
paras: This course has already described meridians as mapped patterns of connection rather than physical pipes, and acupuncture as one way of interacting with that map by pressing a specific point. There's a second, entirely different way of interacting with the same map: movement. A category of practice sometimes called "guided stretching along the meridians" designs specific stretches, twists, and postures to trace the exact path of a chosen meridian through the body, rather than stretching muscles in whatever shape feels convenient.

The logic follows directly from what this unit has already covered about the twelve meridians running along the inner or outer surface of each limb. A stretch that extends the inner arm from shoulder to fingertip, palm rotated outward, follows the same path this course earlier assigned to the Lung meridian; a stretch reaching down the back of the leg follows a path associated with the Bladder meridian. The claim isn't that stretching a muscle group and "moving qi along a meridian" are two different physical events — it's that describing the same movement through the meridian map adds a layer of intention and attention that plain stretching, done without that map in mind, doesn't include.

This connects two things this course has kept mostly separate until now: the passive picture of meridians as something a practitioner presses from the outside, and an active picture of a person moving their own body along that same map. Read together, they suggest that meridians were never meant to describe only what a doctor does to a patient — they were also meant to describe what a person could learn to do for themselves.
paras_zh: 這門課已經把經絡描述成一種被繪製出來的連結模式，而不是實體管線，也把針灸描述成一種透過按壓特定的點來與這張地圖互動的方式。還有第二種、完全不同的方式，能跟同一張地圖互動：動作。有一類練習，有時被稱為「循經導引」，設計了特定的伸展、扭轉與姿勢，來描繪出一條選定的經絡在身體裡確切的路徑，而不是用任何感覺方便的形狀來伸展肌肉。

這個邏輯直接延續自這個單元稍早提過的、十二經絡沿著每個肢體內側或外側表面走的內容。一個從肩膀延伸到指尖、手掌向外翻轉的手臂內側伸展，走的正是這門課稍早分配給肺經的同一條路徑；一個沿著腿部後側往下伸展的動作，走的是跟膀胱經有關的路徑。這裡的主張不是說伸展一組肌肉跟「沿著經絡推動氣」是兩件不同的物理事件——而是說，透過經絡地圖來描述同一個動作，加上了一層單純伸展、沒有把這張地圖放在心上時所沒有的意圖與專注。
這連結起這門課到目前為止大致分開處理的兩件事：把經絡當成一種醫師從外部按壓的被動圖像，以及一個人沿著同一張地圖移動自己身體的主動圖像。合在一起讀，它們暗示著經絡從來不是只用來描述醫師對病人做了什麼——它們也被用來描述一個人可以學會為自己做什麼。

lessons.blurb_zh: 當朋友問「如果經絡是真的，為什麼核磁共振找不到？」，一段整合這個單元的示範回答。
paras: Suppose a friend asks, "If meridians are real, why can't doctors find them with an MRI?" This question deserves a direct, honest answer rather than a defensive one: "You're right that no meridian shows up as a distinct physical structure. Chinese medicine doesn't actually claim it will — a meridian describes a mapped pattern of connection and influence between body regions, built from centuries of clinical observation, not a physical tube waiting to be found."

A concrete example helps more than an abstract defense: "Think about referred pain — the way a heart attack can cause pain down the left arm. Western medicine explains that through shared nerve pathways. Chinese medicine noticed the exact same connection centuries earlier and mapped it as the Heart meridian. Two very different systems, arriving at a similar observation through different methods — that's a better way to think about meridians than 'invisible pipes.'"

Finally, it's worth being clear about where the explanation stops: "Acupuncture points are specific spots along these mapped connections, and using them safely takes years of training — it's not something to try on your own after reading about it. If you're curious enough to actually try acupuncture, the answer is the same as every lesson in this course: find a licensed, trained practitioner."
paras_zh: 假設一位朋友問：「如果經絡是真的，為什麼醫師沒辦法用核磁共振找到它？」這個問題值得一個直接、誠實的回答，而不是防衛性的回答：「你說得對，沒有任何一條經絡會以一個明確的物理結構出現。中醫其實也不主張它會被找到——經絡描述的是身體區域之間一種被繪製出來的連結與影響模式，是好幾個世紀臨床觀察累積出來的，不是一根等著被找到的實體管子。」
一個具體的例子，會比抽象的辯護更有幫助：「想想牽涉痛——心臟病發作為什麼會痛到左手臂。西醫用共享的神經路徑來解釋這件事。中醫在好幾個世紀以前，就注意到完全相同的連結，並把它畫成了心經。兩套非常不同的系統，透過不同的方法，抵達了類似的觀察——這比『看不見的管子』是理解經絡更好的方式。」
最後，值得講清楚這個解釋在哪裡打住：「穴位是沿著這些被繪製出來的連結上的特定點，安全地使用它們需要好幾年的訓練——讀完這篇文章之後，不是可以自己嘗試的事。如果你真的好奇想試針灸，答案跟這門課每一課一樣：找一位合格且受過訓練的醫師。」

According to the passage, what concrete example is used to make meridians less abstract for the friend?

answers: Because it's true that no meridian shows up as a distinct physical structure, and Chinese medicine doesn't actually claim it will — being upfront about this is more honest than being defensive.
Referred pain from a heart attack, which causes pain down the left arm — a pattern Western medicine explains through nerve pathways and that Chinese medicine mapped earlier as the Heart meridian.
That it's not something to try on your own — using acupuncture points safely takes years of training, and anyone curious should find a licensed, trained practitioner.

units.title_en: Unit 6: Six Excesses and Seven Emotions
units.blurb_en: How weather attacks from outside, and emotion disturbs from inside — two causes, one shared logic.
units.blurb_zh: 天氣如何從外部攻擊，情緒如何從內部擾亂——兩種成因，同一套邏輯。

lessons.title: Six Excesses: When the Weather Attacks
lessons.blurb_en: Wind, cold, heat, dampness, dryness, fire — six environmental patterns Chinese medicine treats as causes of illness.
lessons.blurb_zh: 風寒暑濕燥火——中醫把六種環境模式當成致病的原因。
paras: English already has a phrase that captures part of what Chinese medicine calls the "six excesses": "catching a chill." Most English speakers use this loosely, without really believing that cold weather itself causes illness rather than the germs that happen to spread more easily in it. Chinese medicine takes the idea more literally and more systematically, describing six environmental patterns — wind, cold, heat, dampness, dryness, and fire — as external factors capable of invading the body directly and causing a recognizable pattern of illness.

Each of the six has its own signature. Cold tends to cause contraction, stiffness, and pain that eases with warmth. Dampness tends to cause heaviness, sluggishness, and symptoms that are slow to resolve, the way damp air itself feels heavy and lingers. Heat and fire tend to cause redness, rapid onset, and a feeling of being overheated from within. Dryness tends to cause thirst and irritation of anything moist by nature, such as the throat or skin. Wind — discussed more in the next lesson — tends to cause sudden changes and symptoms that move from place to place.

The word "excess" in "six excesses" doesn't mean these six things are bad in normal amounts — a cold breeze or a humid day is simply weather. They become "excesses" specifically when a person's body is not equipped to handle the exposure, which is why the same weather can leave one person unaffected and another person clearly unwell. It's less a claim about the weather itself and more a claim about the meeting point between weather and a particular body's current resilience.
paras_zh: 英文本身已經有一個片語，捕捉到了中醫「六淫」概念的一部分：「著涼」（catching a chill）。多數英語使用者這樣講的時候，並不是很認真地相信是寒冷的天氣本身造成生病，而不是恰好在那種天氣裡更容易散播的病菌。中醫把這個概念講得更直白、也更有系統：把風、寒、暑、濕、燥、火這六種環境模式，描述成能直接入侵身體、造成一種可辨識的疾病模式的外在因子。
這六種各自有自己的特徵。寒往往造成收縮、僵硬，還有遇溫暖就緩解的疼痛。濕往往造成沉重感、遲滯，還有慢慢才會好轉的症狀，就像潮濕的空氣本身讓人覺得沉重、久久不散。暑跟火往往造成發紅、發作快速，還有一種從體內發熱的感覺。燥往往造成口渴，還有任何本質濕潤的部位（像喉嚨或皮膚）感到刺激不適。風——下一課會更詳細討論——往往造成突然的變化，還有到處遊走的症狀。
「六淫」裡的「淫」（過度）這個字，不代表這六樣東西在正常份量下是壞的——一陣涼風或一個潮濕的日子，本來就只是天氣而已。它們變成「淫」（過度），特別是在一個人的身體沒有能力應付那次暴露的時候，這也是為什麼同樣的天氣，可以讓一個人完全沒事，卻讓另一個人明顯不舒服。這與其說是對天氣本身的主張，不如說是天氣跟一個人目前的抵抗力之間，那個相遇點的主張。

answers: "Catching a chill" — most English speakers use it loosely, without really believing cold weather itself causes illness rather than germs that spread more easily in it.
Heaviness, sluggishness, and symptoms that are slow to resolve, the way damp air itself feels heavy and lingers.
It depends on the meeting point between the weather and a particular body's current resilience, not on the weather alone.

lessons.title: Wind Is the Spearhead of All Diseases
lessons.blurb_en: Why sudden, shifting symptoms get blamed on "wind" — and why that's a useful category, not a superstition.
lessons.blurb_zh: 為什麼突然、會移動的症狀會被歸咎於「風」——以及這為什麼是一個有用的類別，不是迷信。
paras: Among the six excesses introduced in the last lesson, Chinese medicine singles out wind for special attention, calling it "the spearhead of the hundred diseases" — the factor most likely to lead an attack and open the way for others to follow. The reasoning is based on a simple physical observation: wind moves things, changes direction suddenly, and rarely travels alone. In Chinese medicine's logic, an illness that behaves the same way — appearing suddenly, shifting location, or changing character quickly — is read as carrying a "wind" pattern, whether or not actual weather was involved.

This is why wind is described as "the spearhead": cold, dampness, or heat rarely invade the body cleanly on their own. They are said to ride in on wind, the way dust and pollen travel on an actual breeze. A "wind-cold" pattern, for example, describes an illness with wind's suddenness and cold's contraction and chill combined — closer to what English speakers mean by the early, sudden stage of catching a common cold than to a philosophical metaphor.

The practical value of "wind" as a category is that it gives Chinese medicine a name for a recognizable clinical picture: rapid onset, symptoms that move (a headache that shifts location, joint pain that travels from one joint to another), and an illness that seems to arrive from nowhere. Whether or not modern science would classify the cause the same way, the pattern being described — sudden, moving, and rarely isolated — is a genuinely useful thing to notice and name.
paras_zh: 在上一課介紹的六淫裡，中醫特別挑出風來重點討論，稱它為「百病之長」——最可能帶頭發動攻擊、為其他病邪打開道路的因子。這個推理立基於一個簡單的物理觀察：風會讓東西移動、突然改變方向，而且很少單獨行動。在中醫的邏輯裡，一種表現得同樣——突然出現、位置轉移，或性質快速改變——的疾病，會被讀成帶有「風」的模式，不管實際的天氣有沒有牽涉在內。
這就是為什麼風被稱為「百病之長」：寒、濕或熱，很少乾乾淨淨地單獨入侵身體。它們被認為是搭著風的便車進來的，就像塵埃和花粉搭著實際的風移動一樣。舉例來說，「風寒」的模式描述的是一種結合了風的突然性與寒的收縮、發冷的疾病——這比較接近英語使用者所說的普通感冒早期、突然發作的階段，而不是一個哲學上的比喻。
「風」作為一個類別的實際價值，是它給了中醫一個名字，來稱呼一種可辨識的臨床表現：發作快速、症狀會移動（頭痛的位置會轉移、關節痛從一個關節跑到另一個關節），還有一種疾病感覺像是憑空冒出來的。不論現代科學會不會用同樣的方式來分類這個成因，這裡被描述的模式——突然、會移動、很少單獨出現——本身就是一件真正值得注意並命名的事。

It gives Chinese medicine a name for a recognizable clinical picture — rapid onset, symptoms that move, and an illness that seems to arrive from nowhere — which is a useful thing to notice and name regardless of how modern science classifies the cause.

lessons.title: The Seven Emotions
lessons.blurb_en: Anger, joy, worry, sadness, grief, fear, fright — seven emotions, each matched to an organ they can injure in excess.
lessons.blurb_zh: 怒喜思悲憂恐驚——七種情緒，每一種過度時都對應著一個可能受傷的臟腑。
paras: Alongside the six excesses, which attack from outside, Chinese medicine describes seven emotions capable of causing illness from inside: anger, joy, worry, sadness, grief, fear, and fright. The claim isn't that having emotions is dangerous — feeling angry or afraid occasionally is a normal, healthy response to life. The claim is that any one of these seven, when sustained at an extreme level over time, can injure a specific organ, the same way any of the six excesses can, just from the inside rather than the outside.

Each emotion is matched to a zang organ from earlier in this course, following the same five-element logic. Anger is said to injure the liver. Excessive joy — meaning overstimulation, not ordinary happiness — is said to injure the heart. Worry and pensiveness are said to injure the spleen. Sadness and grief are said to injure the lung. Fear is said to injure the kidney. A person under prolonged anger developing digestive trouble, or a person under prolonged grief developing shortness of breath, is showing exactly the pattern this framework predicts.

This is not a claim that emotions are the only cause of illness, nor that feeling a difficult emotion once will damage an organ. The seven emotions become a medical concern the same way the six excesses do: not through a single instance, but through a sustained, extreme pattern that the body isn't given enough time or support to recover from.
paras_zh: 除了從外部攻擊的六淫之外，中醫還描述了能從內部造成疾病的七種情緒：怒、喜、思、悲、憂、恐、驚。這裡的主張不是「有情緒就是危險的」——偶爾感到生氣或害怕，是對人生正常、健康的反應。這裡的主張是，這七種情緒裡的任何一種，如果長時間維持在極端的程度，就能傷害一個特定的臟腑，跟六淫能造成的傷害一樣，只是從內部而不是從外部而已。
每一種情緒都對應到這門課前面介紹過的一個臟腑，遵循同一套五行的邏輯。怒被認為會傷肝。過度的喜——意思是過度的刺激，不是一般的快樂——被認為會傷心。思與憂被認為會傷脾。悲與憂被認為會傷肺。恐被認為會傷腎。一個長期處在憤怒中的人出現消化問題，或一個長期處在悲傷中的人出現呼吸急促，展現的正是這個框架所預測的模式。
這不是在主張情緒是疾病唯一的成因，也不是說感受一次困難的情緒就會傷害一個臟腑。七情變成醫療上的顧慮，跟六淫一樣：不是透過單一一次的事件，而是透過一個持續、極端、身體沒有得到足夠時間或支持去恢復的模式。

lessons.title: When Emotion Becomes the Cause, Not Just the Feeling
lessons.blurb_en: Anger makes qi rise, fear makes it sink — why "calm down" rarely works, and what actually might.
lessons.blurb_zh: 怒讓氣上升，恐讓氣下沉——為什麼叫人「冷靜下來」通常沒用，什麼才可能真的有用。
paras: The last lesson matched each of the seven emotions to an organ it can injure, but Chinese medicine goes one step further, describing exactly how an emotion causes damage: through its effect on the movement of qi. Anger is said to make qi rise — which is why prolonged anger is associated with headaches, a flushed face, and a pounding sensation, all symptoms of qi surging upward. Fear is said to make qi descend and scatter — which is why sudden, intense fear is associated with a sinking feeling in the stomach or a loss of bladder control.

Worry and overthinking are said to "knot" qi, causing it to stagnate in one place rather than flow — which shows up as a tight sensation in the chest or stomach, and a struggle to make decisions or move forward. Grief is said to drain qi directly, matching the exhaustion and shortness of breath that so often follow real loss. Joy, in its ordinary form, is said to relax and smooth qi's movement, which is part of why Chinese medicine considers joy protective rather than harmful in typical amounts — it is only sudden, overstimulating joy that is treated as potentially disruptive.

This mechanism explains why the emotional causes of illness in Chinese medicine were never meant to be treated as separate from the physical ones. An emotion isn't just a feeling that happens to accompany a symptom — in this framework, it is a specific, describable disturbance in how qi is moving, with its own physical signature. This is also why simply telling someone to "calm down" does very little: the goal is restoring qi's normal movement, not suppressing the emotion itself.
paras_zh: 上一課把七情裡的每一種，對應到它可能傷害的一個臟腑，但中醫更進一步，描述了情緒到底是怎麼造成傷害的：透過它對氣運行的影響。怒被認為會讓氣上升——這就是為什麼長期的憤怒會跟頭痛、臉紅、跳動感連在一起，這些都是氣往上衝的症狀。恐被認為會讓氣下降並渙散——這就是為什麼突然、強烈的恐懼會跟胃裡一沉的感覺，或膀胱失控連在一起。
思與過度思考被認為會讓氣「結」，讓它停滯在一個地方，而不是流動——這會表現成胸口或胃部的緊繃感，還有難以下決定或往前邁進。悲被認為會直接耗損氣，這對應著真正失去所愛之後常常伴隨而來的疲憊與呼吸急促。喜，在一般的形式下，被認為會讓氣的運行放鬆、順暢，這也是為什麼中醫認為一般份量的喜是保護性的、而不是有害的——只有突然、過度刺激的喜，才會被當成可能造成紊亂的因素。
這個機制解釋了為什麼中醫從來不打算把情緒的致病因素跟身體的致病因素分開來看待。一種情緒不只是恰好伴隨著一個症狀出現的感受——在這個框架裡，它是氣運行上一種具體、可描述的紊亂，有它自己的身體特徵。這也是為什麼只是叫一個人「冷靜下來」幾乎沒什麼用：目標是恢復氣正常的運行，而不是壓抑情緒本身。

answers: Anger is said to make qi rise, matching symptoms like headaches, a flushed face, and a pounding sensation.
Worry and overthinking are said to "knot" qi, causing it to stagnate, matching a tight sensation in the chest or stomach and difficulty making decisions or moving forward.
Because the goal is restoring qi's normal movement, not suppressing the emotion itself — an emotion is a specific, describable disturbance in qi movement, not just a feeling to be silenced.

lessons.title: Damp-Heat: When Two Excesses Team Up
lessons.blurb_en: Dampness alone is sluggish, heat alone is fast — combined, they create a pattern messier than either one on its own.
lessons.blurb_zh: 濕單獨是遲滯的，熱單獨是快速的——兩者合在一起，會產生比任何一種單獨出現都更棘手的模式。
paras: An earlier lesson in this unit described the six excesses as six separate categories, but Chinese medicine recognizes that more than one excess frequently invades together, and one particular combination — damp-heat — is common enough to deserve its own name. Dampness on its own tends to produce heaviness and symptoms slow to resolve; heat on its own tends to produce redness and rapid onset. Combined, they don't simply add together — they interact, the way a lid trapped over a simmering, humid pot produces something different from either steam or heat alone.

This combination is traditionally described using a cooking metaphor: dampness is like water, heat is like fire, and damp-heat is what happens when the two are sealed together in a covered pot — a slow, sticky, hard-to-clear steam rather than a quick boil-off. Symptoms traditionally associated with damp-heat reflect this: skin conditions that are both inflamed and oozing, digestive trouble that is both urgent and sluggish, and a general sensation of being weighed down while also running warm — a combination that neither pure dampness nor pure heat produces on its own.

Recognizing damp-heat as its own category, rather than trying to treat it as dampness with a side of heat, matters because clearing heat alone can dry out and worsen dampness, while draining dampness alone can leave heat with nothing to disperse it. This is a small but clear example of why the six excesses were never meant to be diagnosed one at a time in isolation — patterns combine, and the combined pattern often behaves differently from the sum of its parts.
paras_zh: 這個單元稍早的一課，把六淫描述成六個各自獨立的類別，但中醫也承認，不只一種病邪經常一起入侵，而其中一種特定的組合——濕熱——常見到值得擁有自己的名字。濕單獨出現時，往往產生沉重感、慢慢才會好轉的症狀；熱單獨出現時，往往產生發紅、快速發作。兩者合在一起，不是單純地相加——它們會互相作用，就像一個蓋子蓋在一鍋悶燒、潮濕的鍋子上，會產生跟單純的蒸氣或單純的熱都不一樣的東西。
這種組合傳統上用一個烹飪的比喻來描述：濕像水，熱像火，濕熱就是兩者被密封在一個加蓋的鍋子裡時會發生的事——一種緩慢、黏膩、難以清除的蒸氣，而不是快速蒸發。傳統上跟濕熱有關的症狀，反映了這一點：既發炎又滲液的皮膚問題、既急迫又遲滯的消化問題，還有一種既被壓得沉重、又同時感到燥熱的整體感受——這是純粹的濕或純粹的熱單獨都不會產生的組合。
把濕熱認出成它自己的一個類別，而不是試圖把它當成「濕帶一點熱」來處理，這件事很重要，因為單純清熱可能會讓濕變得更乾、更嚴重，而單純祛濕可能會讓熱失去被分散掉的東西。這是一個小而清楚的例子，說明為什麼六淫從來不打算被一個一個孤立地診斷——模式會組合起來，而組合出來的模式，行為往往跟各個部分加起來不一樣。

lessons.title: Internal Wind vs. External Wind
lessons.blurb_en: The lesson on "wind" earlier in this unit was only half the story — wind can also be generated inside the body, with no weather involved at all.
lessons.blurb_zh: 這個單元稍早關於「風」的那一課只講了一半——風也可以在身體內部生成，完全跟天氣無關。
paras: An earlier lesson in this unit described wind as an external excess — something that invades from outside, often riding in alongside cold or dampness, and behaving the way actual wind behaves: sudden, shifting, rarely alone. Chinese medicine also describes a second, entirely different kind of wind that has nothing to do with weather at all: internal wind, generated inside the body itself, usually as the result of some other imbalance reaching an extreme.

Internal wind is most often linked to an excess of yang or a severe deficiency of yin in the liver, since the liver's smooth, upward-moving qi, when it runs completely unchecked, is said to stir into the same kind of sudden, shifting movement associated with wind generally. The symptoms traditionally linked to internal wind reflect this: dizziness, tremor, and in severe cases, sudden collapse or convulsion — movement-based, "wind-like" symptoms generated from within, rather than caught from without.

The distinction matters because the two require completely different responses. External wind is addressed by expelling the invading excess before it settles in further. Internal wind is addressed by correcting the underlying imbalance — the excess yang or deficient yin — that's generating the wind-like movement in the first place. Treating them the same way, simply because both share the label "wind," would miss that one is an intruder to be removed and the other is a symptom of something already present that has gotten out of hand.
paras_zh: 這個單元稍早的一課，把風描述成一種外來的病邪——一種從外部入侵、常常搭著寒或濕一起進來的東西，表現得跟實際的風一樣：突然、會移動、很少單獨出現。中醫也描述了第二種、完全不同種類的風，跟天氣完全無關：內風，在身體內部自己生成，通常是某個其他失衡達到極端之後的結果。
內風最常被連結到肝的陽亢或陰的嚴重不足，因為肝那種順暢、向上運行的氣，一旦完全不受約束地運行，被認為會攪動成跟一般的風有關的那種突然、會移動的動作。傳統上跟內風連結的症狀，反映了這一點：頭暈、顫抖，嚴重的情況下，突然的昏倒或抽搐——這些是以動作為基礎、「像風一樣」的症狀，是從身體內部生成的，不是從外面感染來的。
這個區分很重要，因為兩者需要完全不同的應對方式。外風的處理方式，是在它進一步安頓下來之前，把入侵的病邪驅趕出去。內風的處理方式，是修正一開始造成這種風樣運動的根本失衡——過盛的陽或不足的陰。只因為兩者都共享「風」這個標籤就用同樣的方式處理，會忽略掉一個是該被移除的入侵者，另一個是某個已經存在、失控了的東西所產生的一個症狀。

answers: External wind invades from outside, riding in with cold or dampness like actual weather; internal wind is generated inside the body itself, usually as the result of another imbalance reaching an extreme.
An excess of yang or severe deficiency of yin in the liver; it traditionally produces dizziness, tremor, and in severe cases, sudden collapse or convulsion.

lessons.title: The Body Remembers: How Old Emotional Patterns Show Up Physically
lessons.blurb_en: A single burst of anger passes. Years of it, this course's framework suggests, can leave a mark long after the feeling itself is gone.
lessons.blurb_zh: 一次的憤怒會過去。這門課的框架認為，好幾年的憤怒，會在感受本身消失之後，留下長期的痕跡。
paras: An earlier lesson in this unit described how a single emotion, in excess, can disturb qi in a specific, describable way — anger raising it, fear sinking it, worry knotting it. What that lesson didn't fully address is what happens when the emotional pattern isn't a single event but a habit repeated for years, and the answer this course's framework gives is that the disturbance can outlast the feeling that caused it, settling into the body as a lasting pattern rather than a passing one.

A person who spent a decade in a high-conflict job, for instance, may no longer feel angry on a given day, yet still carry the physical pattern that years of frequent anger left behind — a liver qi that stays slightly too eager to move, showing up as a short temper triggered by small annoyances, or a tendency toward tension headaches that has nothing to do with that day's mood at all. The emotion that built the pattern is gone; the pattern it built remains.

This is part of why this course has repeatedly separated "an emotion" from "a physical pattern with that emotion's signature," rather than treating them as the same thing. A person can present with a liver-qi pattern while reporting they don't feel angry at all — the felt emotion and the bodily disturbance it once caused have become two different things, on two different timelines, and addressing only the mood a person reports in the moment misses the pattern that outlasted it.
paras_zh: 這個單元稍早的一課，描述了單一一種情緒過度時，能以一種具體、可描述的方式擾亂氣——怒讓氣上升，恐讓氣下沉，思讓氣打結。那一課沒有完全談到的是，當這種情緒模式不是單一一次事件，而是重複好幾年的習慣時，會發生什麼事，而這門課的框架給的答案是：這種擾亂可能會比造成它的那個感受活得更久，在身體裡安頓成一個持續存在的模式，而不是一個過去式的模式。
舉例來說，一個在高衝突的工作裡待了十年的人，或許在某一天已經不再感到憤怒，卻仍然帶著多年頻繁憤怒留下的身體模式——一種稍微太急著往外衝的肝氣，表現成被小小的煩擾就觸發的短暫脾氣，或是一種跟那天的心情完全無關的緊張性頭痛傾向。造成這個模式的那個情緒已經消失了；它建立起來的那個模式卻留了下來。
這是為什麼這門課一再把「一種情緒」跟「帶著那種情緒特徵的一種身體模式」分開來看待，而不是把它們當成同一件事的一部分原因。一個人可能呈現出肝氣的模式，卻回報自己一點也不覺得憤怒——那個被感受到的情緒，跟它曾經造成的身體擾亂，已經變成兩件不同的事，在兩條不同的時間軸上，只處理一個人當下回報的心情，會漏掉那個比心情活得更久的模式。

A liver qi that stays slightly too eager to move, showing up as a short temper triggered by small annoyances or a tendency toward tension headaches unrelated to that day's mood.

Because the felt emotion and the bodily disturbance it once caused can become two different things on two different timelines — a person can show a physical pattern while reporting they don't feel that emotion at all, so addressing only the reported mood misses the lasting pattern.

lessons.title: Explaining Six Excesses and Seven Emotions to a Friend
lessons.blurb_en: A model answer for "So Chinese medicine thinks weather and feelings literally cause disease?"
lessons.blurb_zh: 當朋友問「所以中醫真的認為天氣跟情緒會導致疾病？」，一段整合這個單元的示範回答。
paras: Suppose a friend, hearing about the six excesses and seven emotions, asks, "So Chinese medicine thinks weather and feelings literally cause disease?" A precise answer avoids overclaiming: "Not exactly 'cause' in the germ-theory sense. Think of them as recognized risk patterns — the six excesses describe how environmental stress (cold, damp, wind) can overwhelm a body that isn't equipped to handle it, and the seven emotions describe how a sustained, extreme emotional state can disturb the body's functions from the inside, the same way chronic stress is now understood in Western medicine to affect the immune system and digestion."

A concrete comparison helps here too: "It's a bit like saying, 'stress causes ulcers.' That's not one single germ causing a single disease — it's a real, documented pattern where a sustained internal state changes how the body functions, making certain problems more likely. Chinese medicine just built its own detailed map of which sustained states connect to which physical patterns, using its own vocabulary — wind, qi rising, qi knotting — instead of the vocabulary Western medicine developed later."

It's worth ending, as always, on the practical boundary: "None of this means you can diagnose yourself by matching a mood to an organ. It means Chinese medicine takes seriously something a lot of modern medicine is only recently taking seriously too — that sustained emotional states have real physical effects. For an actual health concern, the answer is still the same: see a licensed doctor."
paras_zh: 假設一位朋友聽到六淫七情，問：「所以中醫真的認為天氣跟情緒會導致疾病？」一個精確的回答，要避免誇大：「不完全是細菌致病論那種意義上的『導致』。可以把它們想成已被認可的風險模式——六淫描述的是環境壓力（寒、濕、風）怎麼壓垮一個沒有能力應付的身體；七情描述的是一種持續、極端的情緒狀態，怎麼從內部擾亂身體的功能，就像現在西醫也理解慢性壓力會影響免疫系統和消化功能一樣。」
這裡有一個具體的比喻會有幫助：「這有點像是說『壓力導致潰瘍』。那不是單一一種細菌造成單一一種疾病——那是一個真實、有紀錄的模式，一種持續的內在狀態改變了身體運作的方式，讓某些問題更容易發生。中醫只是用它自己的詞彙——風、氣上升、氣結——建立了自己一套詳細的地圖，說明哪些持續的狀態連結到哪些身體模式，而不是用西醫後來發展出來的詞彙。」
值得像往常一樣，用實際的界線來收尾：「這一切不代表你可以靠把一種心情對應到一個臟腑，來自我診斷。這代表中醫認真看待一件事——而現代醫學最近也才開始認真看待這件事——就是持續的情緒狀態，真的會有身體上的影響。真的有健康疑慮的話，答案還是一樣：去看合格醫師。」

lessons.title: Why Chinese Medicine Has 24 Seasons, Not 4
lessons.title_zh: 為什麼中醫用二十四節氣，不是四季
lessons.blurb_en: Why "eat warm foods in winter" is too vague to be useful — and what a fifteen-day calendar fixes.
lessons.blurb_zh: 為什麼「冬天吃溫熱食物」太籠統沒有用——以及一套十五天曆法怎麼修正這件事。
paras: English divides the year into four seasons, and most health advice that mentions seasons at all stays just as broad — "eat warm foods in winter," "stay hydrated in summer." Chinese medicine divides the year into twenty-four solar terms instead, each lasting roughly fifteen days and marking the sun's precise position along its yearly path. The difference isn't decorative. A piece of advice meant to cover a three-month season is almost always too vague to be useful; a piece of advice tied to a fifteen-day window can be specific enough to actually follow.

Each solar term carries its own name and its own expected pattern of change — some mark shifts in temperature, like "slight cold" and "great cold" in the depths of winter; some mark shifts in the visible world, like "insects awaken" in early spring, when hibernating creatures are said to stir; some mark agricultural turning points, like "grain in ear," once used to time the harvest. The names function like fifteen-day chapter headings for the year, each one flagging a specific transition worth adjusting for.

For someone learning to apply Chinese medicine's ideas about qi, yin-yang, and the organs to daily life, the twenty-four solar terms are the actual calendar the whole system runs on. Advice like "protect the liver's smooth qi in spring" only becomes useful once it's anchored to a specific window of weeks, rather than left floating across an entire season three months long.
paras_zh: 英文把一年分成四季，而大部分連季節都會提到的健康建議，也就停留在同樣籠統的層次——「冬天吃溫熱的食物」、「夏天要補充水分」。中醫把一年分成二十四個節氣，每個大約十五天，標記太陽在一年運行路徑上的精確位置。這個差別不是裝飾性的。一則要涵蓋整整三個月一個季節的建議，幾乎必然太模糊、沒辦法真的照著做；一則綁定在一個十五天窗口的建議，可以具體到真正能被執行。
每個節氣都有自己的名字，以及自己被預期的變化模式——有些標記溫度的轉變，像深冬的「小寒」跟「大寒」；有些標記可見世界的轉變，像早春的「驚蟄」，這時候冬眠的生物被認為開始甦醒；有些標記農業上的轉折點，像曾經用來抓收成時機的「芒種」。這些名字的功能，就像一年份、每十五天一個章節的標題，每一個都標出一個值得為它調整生活的具體轉變。
對一個正在學習把氣、陰陽、臟腑這些中醫概念應用到日常生活的人來說，二十四節氣是這整套系統實際運行的曆法。像「春天要保護肝的順暢之氣」這種建議，只有把它綁定在一個具體的、以週為單位的窗口，而不是任它漂浮在一整個長達三個月的季節裡，才會真正變得有用。

lessons.title: Living with the Body's Organ Clock
lessons.blurb_en: Why sleeping before eleven matters, and why an afternoon headache might be a clue, not a coincidence.
lessons.blurb_zh: 為什麼十一點前睡覺很重要，以及為什麼每天下午的頭痛可能是線索，不是巧合。
paras: Chinese medicine describes a twenty-four-hour cycle in which each of twelve two-hour periods is associated with peak activity in a particular organ, following the same twelve meridians introduced earlier in this course. The pattern is often called the organ clock, and it gives a time-based answer to a question this course has asked from several angles: not just what an organ does, but when it's doing its most important work.

A few points on this clock carry the most practical weight. The period from eleven at night to one in the morning is associated with the gallbladder, and from one to three in the morning with the liver — together considered the window in which blood is renewed and detoxified most efficiently, which is the basis for this course's earlier advice to sleep before eleven. The period from five to seven in the morning is associated with the large intestine, offering a time-based explanation for why a morning bowel movement is considered a healthy sign rather than a coincidence.

The organ clock isn't a rule that a person must be awake or asleep at exact minutes to stay healthy — bodies and schedules vary, and rigid anxiety about the clock defeats its purpose. Its real use is as a rough map: symptoms that reliably show up at the same time of day (a headache every afternoon, a cough that worsens every night) are treated as a meaningful clue pointing toward a specific organ's current state, not treated as a random coincidence of timing.
paras_zh: 中醫描述了一個二十四小時的循環，其中十二個各兩小時的時段，分別對應到某個臟腑活動的高峰期，遵循的正是這門課稍早介紹過的十二經絡。這個模式常被稱為臟腑時鐘，它給了這門課從好幾個角度問過的一個問題一個以時間為基礎的答案：不只是一個臟腑做什麼，還有它什麼時候做最重要的工作。
這個時鐘上有幾個點特別有實際的份量。晚上十一點到凌晨一點對應到膽，凌晨一點到三點對應到肝——這兩者合起來被認為是血液被最有效率地更新與解毒的窗口，這也是這門課稍早建議十一點前睡覺的依據。早上五點到七點對應到大腸，用時間的角度解釋了為什麼早晨排便被認為是一個健康的徵象，而不是巧合。
臟腑時鐘不是一條「必須在精確的分鐘睡著或醒來才能保持健康」的規則——每個人的身體與作息各不相同，對時鐘過度焦慮反而違背了它的用意。它真正的用處，是當成一張粗略的地圖：可靠地在一天中同一個時段出現的症狀（每天下午的頭痛、每晚加重的咳嗽），會被當成指向某個臟腑目前狀態的一個有意義的線索，而不是當成時間上隨機的巧合。

lessons.title: Spring: Encouraging Growth Without Forcing It
lessons.blurb_en: Sleep later, rise earlier, walk loosely, and don't bottle up frustration — spring's advice, all pointing one direction.
lessons.blurb_zh: 晚睡早起、穿寬鬆的衣服散步、別悶住挫折感——春天的建議，全部指向同一個方向。
paras: Spring is matched to wood and the liver in the five-element framework introduced earlier in this course, and Chinese medicine's classic advice for the season follows directly from that match: the season's job is encouraging growth, not forcing it. The Yellow Emperor's Inner Classic recommends going to bed a little later and rising earlier in spring, then taking a walk in loose, comfortable clothing — letting the body's energy stretch outward and upward the way new shoots do, rather than staying wrapped up and contracted as in winter.

The emotional advice for spring follows the same logic. Because anger is matched to the liver, and the liver governs smooth, unobstructed qi flow, spring is considered a season when suppressed frustration does particular damage — qi that wants to move outward, like a spring shoot, but is blocked, builds pressure with nowhere to go. The classic recommendation isn't to avoid strong feelings entirely, but to avoid bottling them, and to give the mood room to move the way the season itself is moving.

None of this is about performing enthusiasm on command. It's about not working against a direction the season and the body are already leaning toward. A person forcing themselves to stay indoors, wrapped tightly, holding in frustration during spring is, in this framework, fighting the season on every front at once — physical posture, activity level, and emotional expression, all pointed the wrong way at the same time.
paras_zh: 春天在這門課稍早介紹的五行框架裡對應到木與肝，中醫對這個季節的經典建議，正是直接從這個對應而來：這個季節的任務是鼓勵生長，而不是強迫它。《黃帝內經》建議春天晚一點睡、早一點起，然後穿著寬鬆舒適的衣服去散步——讓身體的能量像新生的嫩芽一樣往外、往上伸展，而不是像冬天那樣裹得緊緊的、收縮著。
春天的情緒建議遵循著同一套邏輯。因為怒對應到肝，而肝主導氣順暢、不受阻礙地流動，春天被認為是一個壓抑的挫折感會造成特別傷害的季節——想要像春天的嫩芽一樣往外移動的氣，卻被堵住，會累積壓力卻無處可去。經典的建議不是要完全避免強烈的感受，而是不要把它們悶住，並且讓心情有空間，跟著這個季節本身移動的方向移動。
這一切都不是在講表演出來的、按指令展現的熱情。它講的是不要跟季節與身體本來就傾向的方向對著幹。一個在春天強迫自己待在室內、把自己裹得緊緊的、把挫折感悶在心裡的人，在這個框架下，是在同一時間、從每一個方向對抗這個季節——身體姿態、活動量、情緒表達，全部同時指向錯誤的方向。

lessons.title: Winter: Storing Rather Than Spending
lessons.blurb_en: Sleep late, wait for the sun, and stop draining what you'll need later — winter's advice, read as one idea.
lessons.blurb_zh: 晚起、等太陽出來、別耗盡以後會需要的東西——冬天的建議，其實是同一個概念。
paras: Winter is matched to water and the kidney in the five-element framework, and its classic advice runs in the opposite direction from spring's: the season's job is storing, not spending. The Yellow Emperor's Inner Classic recommends going to bed early and rising late in winter, "waiting for the sunlight" rather than rising in the dark — the reverse of spring's instruction to rise early, and a direct match to water's pattern of stillness, depth, and conservation.

The same logic extends to physical activity and sweat. Because the kidney is said to store a person's inherited constitutional strength, and because excessive sweating was described earlier in this course as something that drains qi directly, winter is considered a poor season for intense exercise that produces heavy sweating. Moderate movement is still encouraged, but the classic advice draws a clear line between staying active and deliberately draining the body's reserves during the season meant for building them back up.

The emotional dimension follows the pattern too: winter is associated with fear, matched to the kidney, and the classic advice is neither to chase excitement nor to dwell in anxiety, but to keep the mind as calm and settled as the season itself — closer to quiet contentment than to either fear or forced cheerfulness. Winter's entire set of instructions, read together, describes one coherent posture: conserve now, so there is something to spend later.
paras_zh: 冬天在五行框架裡對應到水與腎，它的經典建議跟春天走的方向剛好相反：這個季節的任務是儲藏，而不是支出。《黃帝內經》建議冬天早睡晚起，「必待日光」——等太陽出來再起床，而不是摸黑就起——這跟春天早起的指示正好相反，也直接對應著水靜止、深沉、保存的模式。
同樣的邏輯延伸到身體活動與流汗上。因為腎被認為儲藏著一個人先天的體質根本，而過度流汗在這門課稍早被描述成一種會直接耗損氣的事，冬天被認為不適合做會大量出汗的劇烈運動。適度的活動仍然被鼓勵，但經典的建議清楚劃出一條界線：在一個本該用來把身體的儲備補回來的季節裡，「維持活動」跟「刻意耗盡身體的儲備」是兩件不同的事。
情緒的面向也遵循同樣的模式：冬天跟恐懼有關，對應到腎，而經典的建議既不是去追求刺激，也不是沉溺於焦慮，而是讓心保持像這個季節本身一樣的平靜與安定——比較接近安靜的滿足，而不是恐懼或勉強擠出來的開朗。冬天的整套指示，合在一起讀，描述的是同一種一致的姿態：現在保存起來，以後才有東西可以支出。

lessons.title: Summer: Venting Heat Without Losing Everything With It
lessons.blurb_en: Summer's job is the opposite of winter's — but venting heat and fluid too freely creates its own kind of exhaustion.
lessons.blurb_zh: 夏天的任務跟冬天相反——但把熱和津液都放得太乾脆，會製造出屬於夏天自己的一種耗竭。
paras: Summer is matched to fire and the heart in the five-element framework, and its classic advice continues the arc this course's seasonal unit has followed from spring's growth to winter's storage: summer's job is full, outward growth, the peak of the yang half of the year. The Yellow Emperor's Inner Classic recommends rising early and going to bed a little later, similar to spring, but adds something spring didn't need: a caution against holding in frustration or resentment, described as letting qi "vent" freely the way summer's heat vents outward, rather than bottling it up during the season most associated with open, outward expression.

The physical caution for summer runs alongside the emotional one: because heat and sweating both drain qi and fluids directly, a concept covered in an earlier unit, summer creates a specific risk of losing too much of both at once. A person who sweats heavily through a hot day without adequately replacing fluids can end up with a combined qi-and-fluid deficiency by evening — tired, thirsty, and drained in a way that a cool room and a glass of water only partly fixes.

This is why summer's advice isn't simply "stay active and let things out," despite that being the season's basic direction. It's closer to "let things out, but track what's leaving with them" — venting frustration is encouraged, but venting fluids and qi without replacing them is not, and the two cautions sit side by side precisely because summer is the one season where a person can overdo the very thing the season is supposed to encourage.
paras_zh: 夏天在五行框架裡對應到火與心，它的經典建議延續著這門課節氣單元從春天的生長到冬天的儲藏一路走過來的弧線：夏天的任務是完全、向外的生長，是一年裡陽氣的高峰。《黃帝內經》建議早起、晚一點睡，跟春天類似，但加上了一件春天不需要的提醒：不要壓抑挫折或怨恨，而是要讓氣自由地「宣洩」，就像夏天的熱氣向外散發一樣，而不是在這個最跟開放、向外表達連結的季節裡把它悶住。
夏天在身體上的提醒，跟情緒上的提醒並行：因為熱與流汗都會直接耗損氣與津液，這是稍早一個單元提過的概念，夏天造成一個特定的風險——同時失去太多這兩者。一個在炎熱的一天裡大量流汗、卻沒有適度補充水分的人，到了傍晚可能會落入一種氣與津液合併不足的狀態——疲倦、口渴、耗竭到一間涼爽的房間跟一杯水只能部分解決的程度。
這就是為什麼夏天的建議不是單純的「保持活躍、把東西放出去」，儘管那確實是這個季節的基本方向。它比較接近「該放出去的就放出去，但要追蹤跟著一起流失了什麼」——宣洩挫折感是被鼓勵的，但宣洩津液與氣卻不補回來則不是，這兩個提醒之所以並排出現，正是因為夏天是唯一一個人可能把季節本該鼓勵的那件事做過頭的季節。

lessons.title: Autumn: Gathering In
lessons.blurb_en: After summer's full expansion, autumn's job is the turn inward — and it maps onto the lung and a very specific kind of dryness.
lessons.blurb_zh: 在夏天完全的擴張之後，秋天的任務是轉向內收——它對應著肺，還有一種非常特定的乾燥。
paras: Autumn is matched to metal and the lung in the five-element framework, and it marks the turn from the outward-facing first half of the year to the inward-facing second half. Where spring encourages growth and summer encourages full expansion, autumn's classic advice is about gathering in — the Yellow Emperor's Inner Classic recommends going to bed earlier and rising with the sunrise, keeping the mind calm and the emotions settled rather than scattered, matching a season whose defining image is falling leaves drawing inward and downward rather than a spring shoot reaching out.

Autumn's defining physical challenge, in this framework, is dryness — the season's dominant excess from an earlier unit — and it's matched specifically to the lung, an organ this course has already connected to skin health and the body's outer defenses. Dry air is traditionally thought to injure the lung's own moisture first, showing up as a dry cough, dry skin, and a dry nose or throat that arrives with the season rather than from any illness. The classic response is to eat moistening foods and avoid activities, like excessive sweating, that dry the body further at exactly the time of year it can least afford it.

The emotion matched to autumn is grief, matched to the lung by the same logic covered in the organs unit, and the seasonal advice treats this pairing as reason for gentleness rather than alarm — a normal autumn tendency toward quiet reflection, even mild melancholy, isn't necessarily a problem to fix, but a pattern this framework expects and makes room for, the same way it expects spring's outward energy and winter's quiet. Reading a season's mood as part of its physiology, rather than as separate from it, is the through-line this entire unit has been building toward.
paras_zh: 秋天在五行框架裡對應到金與肺，標記著從一年前半段向外的方向，轉向後半段向內的方向。春天鼓勵生長，夏天鼓勵完全的擴張，秋天的經典建議則是關於內收——《黃帝內經》建議早一點睡、跟著日出起床，讓心保持平靜、情緒保持安定，而不是渙散，對應著這個定義性的意象是落葉向內、向下收攏，而不是春天嫩芽向外伸展的季節。
在這個框架裡，秋天定義性的身體挑戰是燥——這個單元稍早提過、這個季節主導的病邪——它特別對應到肺，這門課已經把肺跟皮膚健康、身體的外部防禦連結起來過。乾燥的空氣傳統上被認為會先傷害肺自己的濕潤，表現成隨著這個季節而來、不是因為任何疾病造成的乾咳、皮膚乾燥，還有鼻子或喉嚨的乾燥。經典的應對方式，是吃滋潤的食物，並避免像過度流汗這種在一年之中身體最負擔不起的時候，讓身體更乾燥的活動。
對應到秋天的情緒是悲，透過臟腑單元講過的同一套邏輯對應到肺，而季節性的建議把這個配對當成溫柔以待、而不是驚慌的理由——秋天一般傾向安靜的沉思，甚至輕微的憂鬱，不必然是一個要修正的問題，而是這個框架預期、並且留出空間容納的一個模式，就像它預期春天向外的活力、冬天的安靜一樣。把一個季節的心情讀成它生理狀態的一部分，而不是跟它分開的東西，是這整個單元一直在建構的那條主線。

answers: Autumn's advice is about gathering in — going to bed earlier, rising with the sunrise, keeping the mind calm and emotions settled — in contrast to spring's advice to encourage outward growth and activity.
Because dry air is traditionally thought to injure the lung's own moisture first, and the lung is already connected to skin health and the body's outer defenses.

lessons.title: Treating Winter's Disease in Summer
lessons.blurb_en: A well-known folk practice built entirely on this course's yin-yang logic: treating a cold-pattern illness during the hottest days of the year.
lessons.blurb_zh: 一個完全建立在這門課陰陽邏輯上的知名民俗做法：在一年最熱的日子裡，治療一個寒性病證。
paras: Among the most well-known applications of the seasonal principles covered in this unit is a practice called "treating winter's disease in summer," most associated with a period called the "three hottest days" — the peak of summer heat, when yang is at its strongest point in the yearly cycle. The idea is to use this narrow window to address conditions that are, by their nature, cold and yang-deficient — chronic conditions that classically worsen in the cold, like certain respiratory and joint conditions — by supporting yang precisely when the surrounding environment is already providing maximum support for it.

The logic follows directly from the seasonal framework covered earlier: this unit's lessons on winter described the season as storing rather than spending, a poor time to be depleting yang further. Summer is nearly the mirror opposite — yang is already at its yearly peak, so a small, well-timed intervention is thought to have outsized leverage, working with the season's direction instead of against it. There's also a corresponding, less famous practice for the opposite direction, sometimes called "treating summer's disease in winter," addressing heat-pattern conditions during winter's peak yin.

What makes this practice worth including at the end of an introductory course is what it reveals about the whole framework this course has built: qi, yin-yang, the organs, and the seasons were never separate topics. Choosing when to act, not only how, is treated as being just as important as the treatment itself — the same seasonal logic that shaped advice about sleep and diet earlier in this unit, applied here to the timing of care.
paras_zh: 這個單元涵蓋的節氣原則裡，最知名的應用之一，叫做「冬病夏治」，最常跟一段叫做「三伏天」的時期連結在一起——夏天最熱的高峰，這時候陽氣在整年的循環裡處在最強的一點。這個想法是利用這個狹窄的窗口，來處理那些本質上屬寒、屬陽虛的狀況——像某些呼吸道與關節方面的慢性病，經典上在寒冷時會惡化——透過在周遭環境已經提供最大支持的時候，去支持陽氣。
這個邏輯直接延續自稍早涵蓋的節氣框架：這個單元關於冬天的課，把這個季節描述成儲藏而不是支出，是一個不適合進一步耗損陽氣的時機。夏天幾乎是完全相反的鏡像——陽氣已經處在整年的高峰，所以一個小的、時機抓得準的介入，被認為能有超乎比例的槓桿作用，順著季節的方向去運作，而不是跟它對抗。也有一個對應的、比較不知名的反方向做法，有時被稱為「夏病冬治」，在冬天陰氣的高峰時，處理屬熱的病證。
讓這個做法值得放進一門入門課程結尾的原因，是它揭示了這門課建構起的整套框架：氣、陰陽、臟腑、節氣，從來不是各自獨立的主題。選擇什麼時候採取行動，不只是怎麼做，被當成跟治療本身一樣重要——這門課稍早塑造了睡眠與飲食建議的同一套節氣邏輯，在這裡被應用到照護的時機上。

Because yang is already at its yearly peak in summer, so a small, well-timed intervention is thought to have outsized leverage, working with the season's direction rather than against it.
That qi, yin-yang, the organs, and the seasons were never separate topics — choosing when to act is treated as just as important as the treatment itself.

lessons.title: Explaining Seasonal Wellness to a Friend
lessons.blurb_en: A model answer for "Isn't that just common sense dressed up in ancient language?"
lessons.blurb_zh: 當朋友問「這不就是包裝成古代語言的常識嗎？」，一段整合這個單元、也整合整門課的示範回答。
paras: Suppose a friend, hearing about spring's "rise early" and winter's "rise late," asks, "Isn't that just common sense dressed up in ancient language?" A fair answer gives credit where it's due: "A lot of it does match common sense — no one's surprised that people feel more energetic in spring and want to hibernate in winter. What Chinese medicine adds isn't the observation itself, but a framework that ties the observation to everything else in this course: spring's energy connects to wood and the liver, winter's conservation connects to water and the kidney, and the same organs, emotions, and qi patterns you've already learned explain why the advice runs in opposite directions."

It also helps to point out what makes the twenty-four solar terms more useful than "common sense": "General seasonal advice is too vague to actually follow — 'eat healthy in summer' doesn't tell you much. A fifteen-day solar term is specific enough to act on, which is closer to a farmer's almanac than to a horoscope. It's less about mysticism and more about a very old, very detailed habit of paying close attention to timing."

The conversation can close on a note that applies to the whole course, not just this unit: "None of this is about performing a ritual on a fixed date. It's about noticing which direction a season is already leaning — toward growth or toward storage — and choosing not to fight it. And as always, real health concerns still belong with a licensed doctor, not a calendar."
paras_zh: 假設一位朋友聽到春天要「早起」、冬天要「晚起」，問：「這不就是包裝成古代語言的常識嗎？」一個公允的回答，該給予它應得的肯定：「有很大一部分確實符合常識——沒有人會驚訝，人在春天會覺得更有活力，在冬天想要冬眠。中醫加進來的，不是這個觀察本身，而是一個把這個觀察跟這門課學過的一切連結起來的框架：春天的活力連結到木與肝，冬天的儲藏連結到水與腎，同一套你已經學過的臟腑、情緒、氣的模式，解釋了為什麼這些建議會朝著相反的方向走。」
指出是什麼讓二十四節氣比「常識」更有用，也會有幫助：「一般的季節性建議太籠統，沒辦法真的照著做——『夏天要吃得健康』告訴不了你什麼具體的事。一個十五天的節氣，具體到可以真正拿來執行，這比較接近農民曆，而不是星座運勢。與其說是神祕主義，不如說是一個非常古老、非常細緻，密切關注時序的習慣。」
這段對話可以用一個適用於整門課、而不只是這個單元的想法來收尾：「這一切都不是在講在固定的日期表演一個儀式。是在注意一個季節已經傾向哪個方向——朝生長，還是朝儲藏——然後選擇不跟它對抗。而一如既往，真正的健康疑慮，還是該交給合格醫師，不是交給一份曆法。」
questions: According to the passage, what does Chinese medicine add to the "common sense" observation that people feel more energetic in spring?
According to the passage, why is a fifteen-day solar term described as "closer to a farmer's almanac than to a horoscope"?
According to the last paragraph, what closing idea does the passage say applies to the whole course, not just this unit?

Because it's specific enough to actually act on, unlike vague seasonal advice, making it more like a practical, detailed calendar than a mystical prediction.
That it's about noticing which direction a season is already leaning and choosing not to fight it — and that real health concerns still belong with a licensed doctor.
